Changes the score tests and adequacy checks propose

Source: R/ctModelImprove.R
ctModelProposals.Rd

Lists the changes ctModelImprove would consider for a fit: the relaxations its score tests indicate and, given an adequacy check, the structural changes the check's families point to (a process of an item's own or shared by two items, a slow process, a cycle, or second order dynamics). Rows can be passed to ctModelImprove(changes = ), which refits with them and judges each by the search's criterion, so that a search can be made one step at a time, by hand.

Usage

ctModelProposals(
  fit,
  score = NULL,
  adequacy = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  relax = c("heterogeneity", "covariates", "statedependence", "volatility", "fixed",
    "level", "slow", "unique", "periodic", "order"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L)
)

Arguments

fit

A fit from ctFit with backend = 'julia'.

score

A ctScoreTest of fit. Run when neither it nor adequacy is given.

adequacy

Optionally a ctFitAdequacy of fit, for the structural changes.

covariates, relax, alpha, cores

As for ctModelImprove.

Value

A data frame of class ctModelProposals, one row per change, strongest first within the relaxations and within the structural changes: change (as a search's history names it), family, p (the evidence ranked by), class, and proposal, what ctModelImprove() needs to make the change.

Details

Every indicated change is listed, including relaxations the tests cannot tell apart (the same class), of which a search round refits only the strongest. The structural changes are listed beside the relaxations, while a search round tries them only once the screen finds nothing.

See also

vignette('score-tests').

Examples

# \donttest{
if (isTRUE(ctJuliaStatus()$available)) {
# A model in which the innovations of the two processes are uncorrelated,
# with the DIFFUSION cell between them fixed at zero.
model <- ctModel(LAMBDA = diag(2),
  manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'), latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'),
  TDpredNames = 'TD1',
  DIFFUSION = matrix(c('diff_eta1', 0, 0, 'diff_eta2'), 2, 2))
fit <- ctFit(ctsemtestdat, model, priors = TRUE)

# The changes the score tests point to, with the p-value each is ranked
# by. Here the score tests propose freeing that covariance.
score <- ctScoreTest(fit)
proposals <- ctModelProposals(fit, score = score)
print(proposals)

# Refit with the first change, and keep it if the likelihood ratio test
# favours it. The history says whether it was kept.
step <- ctModelImprove(fit, changes = proposals[1, ], maxsteps = 1)
print(step$history)

# With an adequacy check as well, the structural changes its families
# point to are listed too, such as a slow process or a cycle.
print(ctModelProposals(fit, score = score, adequacy = ctFitAdequacy(fit)))
}
# }
